prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the stroller and seated child at the bottom edge within roughly 0.3–1 m of the camera wearer, while the adult ahead is about 2–4 m away and the small dog is approximately 2–4 m away, usually to the adult’s right; the parked car is farther right at roughly 4–7 m, with trees, houses, and the road beyond. Across the five frames, the adult and dog become smaller and therefore retreat farther down the driveway, while the stroller remains fixed near the camera; the adult’s orientation changes slightly but remains mostly facing away, so gaze toward the camera cannot be established. Brightness makes near-versus-far relationships clearer than RGB alone, especially the stroller’s strong foreground separation and the layered driveway, street, and background. Absolute metre estimates are uncertain, several regions have smooth or inconsistent depth, object boundaries bleed, and the large bright diagonal surfaces in early frames appear unreliable rather than corresponding cleanly to scene geometry.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates the adult in front, the dog near the adult’s right side, the parked car farther to the right, a potted plant at the far left in the first frame, and foreground people associated with the stroller along the bottom edge. It clarifies overlap and partial visibility: the stroller occupant is heavily cut off by the lower image boundary, the car is clipped at the right edge in later frames, and the dog is small or missing in some frames because it is partly occluded or not detected. Over time, the adult’s mask shifts rightward and becomes slightly smaller as the adult retreats, while the dog stays near the adult; their separation appears roughly 0.5–1.5 m, and both remain several metres beyond the camera wearer’s arm reach. The map is unreliable in the foreground, where the stroller or child is variously mislabeled as person or boat, and it also produces a false tennis-racket label near the dog in the last frame.
descriptions.pose: The pose map shows one main adult skeleton about 2–4 m in front of the camera wearer, initially left of centre and later right of centre, with the body mostly facing away and no reliable evidence of looking toward the camera. The adult’s limbs change configuration across frames as the figure recedes: alternating leg positions indicate forward displacement, while the torso remains upright and turns slightly; no other full body or hand skeleton is reliably recovered. The skeleton makes joint placement, stance, and body orientation easier to read than in RGB, but it provides no direct depth, so distances must be inferred from the RGB and the skeleton’s decreasing image size. The head and extremities are noisy, the yellow marks above the head are malformed, hands are not detected in magenta, and the foreground child, dog, and partially out-of-view stroller receive no usable pose.
